advice.title: Choose how you want to carry your bikes
advice.intro: So how do you decide which bike carrier to buy? To a large extent this is determined by the number of bikes to be carried, and which bike carriers fit your car. Once you have decided which type to go for, consider style, features and price.
bullets: You can fit a tow bar bike carrier to any car that can carry a tow ball
Roof-fitting bike carriers go on any car with a set of roof bars
Rear (back of car) bike carriers are vehicle specific
E-bikes are usually better on a wheel-supported tow bar rack than on the roof

advice.title: Roof mount bike carriers
advice.intro: Sits on your roof bars. You will need one carrier for each bike.
bullets: Carry up to 4 bikes
Holds the bike upright, secure and lockable
Bar and rack package deals available
! Requires roof bars

advice.title: Tow ball mount bike carriers
advice.intro: Fits a standard 50mm tow ball. Easy to use and load, and a strong long-term choice if you carry bikes often.
bullets: Carry up to 4 bikes on one rack
Very secure
Good boot access (choose a tilting model)
Fits all bikes
! Tow bar and tow ball required

advice.title: Hitch mount bike carriers
advice.intro: Slides into a 50mm square hitch receiver. A stable platform for heavier bikes and e-bikes.
bullets: Carry several bikes on one rack
Many tilt or swing away for rear access
! Needs a hitch receiver, not just a tow ball

advice.title: Rear mount bike carriers
advice.intro: Straps to the boot, tailgate or spare wheel. Relatively cheap, but car specific — not suitable for every vehicle.
bullets: Carry up to 3 bikes
! Car specific: not suitable for every vehicle
! Boot access can be tricky

advice.title: Bike carrier accessories
advice.intro: Locks, adaptors, light boards and spares for the carrier you already own.
bullets: Lighting boards and number plate holders
Locks and fitting adaptors
Check the accessory against your existing carrier before ordering

We’ve sourced the best bike carriers from the top rack brands: BUZZRACK, CRUZ, Prorack, Rhino Rack, Thule and Yakima. Bike racks are our specialist subject at Roof Racks Galore, so shop with confidence as our team is with you every step of the way - from pre-sale advice, right through to making sure the bike rack fits safely to your vehicle. “Too easy” as our experts like to say! fitting.heading: Fitting & roof bars
body: Roof-mounted carriers need a set of roof bars.
Tow ball carriers need a tow bar and a standard 50mm tow ball.
Hitch carriers slide into a 50mm square hitch receiver — a tow ball on its own is not enough.
Rear-mounted carriers are vehicle specific, so check the product page before you buy.

items.q: Can I carry an e-bike on a bike rack?
items.a: E-bikes are usually better on a wheel-supported tow ball or hitch rack than on the roof. Use the E-bike compatible filter, and check the product page before you buy.

items.q: Do I need roof bars for a roof-mounted bike rack?
items.a: Yes. Roof-mounted carriers sit on your roof bars, and you will need one carrier for each bike.

items.q: What is the difference between a tow ball and a hitch bike rack?
items.a: A tow ball rack fits a standard 50mm tow ball. A hitch rack slides into a 50mm square hitch receiver, so it needs a hitch receiver, not just a tow ball.

items.q: Are rear-mounted bike racks suitable for every vehicle?
items.a: No. Rear-mounted carriers are vehicle specific, and boot access can be tricky. Check the product page before you buy.
